research_audit.title: Trustee seeks to foreclose $34.4M CMBS loan after alleged first-payment default

reported_facts.fact: A 2026 bond-deal loan allegedly failed on its first payment weeks after being securitized A 2026 bond-deal loan allegedly failed on its first payment weeks after being securitized A commercial mortgage bundled into a 2026 bond deal faces a foreclosure suit, with the trustee alleging the borrowers missed the loan's first payment.

The lawsuit was filed July 28, 2026, in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York by Wilmington Savings Fund Society, FSB, acting as trustee for a commercial-mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) trust called Benchmark 2026-B43.

According to the filing, the loan was originated on or about April 14, 2026, when Barclays Capital Real Estate, the original lender, made a $34,400,000 loan to two borrowers, Milton 90 Pleasant Valley Street LLC and Development Associates of Benton Harbor LLC.
The suit says the note carried a fixed interest rate of 6.400% and ran to a maturity date of May 6, 2036, with payments due on the sixth of each month.
The trustee says it was assigned into the trust effective May 20, 2026, the securitization step that places a loan into a CMBS pool.
It says two of the loan's guarantors filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey on or about June 4, 2026, and that the borrowers missed the first monthly payment, due June 6, 2026.
Under the loan terms, according to the suit, both events counted as defaults, and the interest rate moved to a default rate of 11.400%.
The trustee says it issued a default letter dated June 16, 2026, followed by an acceleration letter dated July 15, 2026, the notice that makes the entire balance due at once.

Once construction is completed — a finish date is set for 2029 — the $2 billion project at 343 Madison Avenue will feature offices, dining spaces, terraces and plenty of amenities.

BXP executives said during Wednesday’s earnings call that the firm is in negotiations with two more prospective tenants, which would bring the building to nearly 70 percent pre-leased.

CEO Owen Thomas said the REIT will lease the rest of the floors closer to delivery to secure “market-leading rents.” “The pricing power in Manhattan remains quite favorable to landlords, and it is expanding geographically,” Hilary Spann, executive vice president of BXP’s New York region, said during the call.

So there’s great strength from the landlord perspective in New York City.” To continue the good news for BXP, the REIT reported approximately 1.8 million square feet of leasing across 106 transactions during the second quarter of 2026, representing roughly 129 percent of the firm’s 10-year average for second-quarter leasing.
The REIT’s second-quarter leasing success was also a significant increase from the 1.1 million square feet of leasing across 68 transactions it reported during the first quarter of this year.

reported_facts.fact: A 2026 bond-deal loan allegedly failed on its first payment weeks after being securitized A 2026 bond-deal loan allegedly failed on its first payment weeks after being securitized A commercial mortgage bundled into a 2026 bond deal faces a foreclosure suit, with the trustee alleging the borrowers missed the loan's first payment.

The lawsuit was filed July 28, 2026, in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York by Wilmington Savings Fund Society, FSB, acting as trustee for a commercial-mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) trust called Benchmark 2026-B43.

According to the filing, the loan was originated on or about April 14, 2026, when Barclays Capital Real Estate, the original lender, made a $34,400,000 loan to two borrowers, Milton 90 Pleasant Valley Street LLC and Development Associates of Benton Harbor LLC.
The suit says the note carried a fixed interest rate of 6.400% and ran to a maturity date of May 6, 2036, with payments due on the sixth of each month.
The trustee says it was assigned into the trust effective May 20, 2026, the securitization step that places a loan into a CMBS pool.
It says two of the loan's guarantors filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey on or about June 4, 2026, and that the borrowers missed the first monthly payment, due June 6, 2026.
Under the loan terms, according to the suit, both events counted as defaults, and the interest rate moved to a default rate of 11.400%.
The trustee says it issued a default letter dated June 16, 2026, followed by an acceleration letter dated July 15, 2026, the notice that makes the entire balance due at once.

BXP, the largest Class A office owner in the country, has landed a $1.2 billion construction loan to build its 930,000-square-foot office tower development at 343 Madison Avenue in Midtown, the real estate investment trust (REIT) announced Wednesday morning during its second-quarter earnings call.
Once construction is completed — a finish date is set for 2029 — the $2 billion project at 343 Madison Avenue will feature offices, dining spaces, terraces and plenty of amenities.
Starr signed a 275,000-square-foot deal in October to anchor the property, and law firm McDermott Will & Schulte took roughly 150,000 square feet there in April.
BXP executives said during Wednesday’s earnings call that the firm is in negotiations with two more prospective tenants, which would bring the building to nearly 70 percent pre-leased.

CEO Owen Thomas said the REIT will lease the rest of the floors closer to delivery to secure “market-leading rents.” “The pricing power in Manhattan remains quite favorable to landlords, and it is expanding geographically,” Hilary Spann, executive vice president of BXP’s New York region, said during the call.

So there’s great strength from the landlord perspective in New York City.” To continue the good news for BXP, the REIT reported approximately 1.8 million square feet of leasing across 106 transactions during the second quarter of 2026, representing roughly 129 percent of the firm’s 10-year average for second-quarter leasing.
The REIT’s second-quarter leasing success was also a significant increase from the 1.1 million square feet of leasing across 68 transactions it reported during the first quarter of this year.
BXP, too, reported funds from operations (FFO) of $283.4 million, or $1.78 per diluted share, for the second quarter, compared to $271.1 million, or $1.71 per share, during the same period last year.

reported_facts.fact: A 2026 bond-deal loan allegedly failed on its first payment weeks after being securitized A 2026 bond-deal loan allegedly failed on its first payment weeks after being securitized A commercial mortgage bundled into a 2026 bond deal faces a foreclosure suit, with the trustee alleging the borrowers missed the loan's first payment.

The lawsuit was filed July 28, 2026, in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York by Wilmington Savings Fund Society, FSB, acting as trustee for a commercial-mortgage-backed securities (CMBS) trust called Benchmark 2026-B43.

According to the filing, the loan was originated on or about April 14, 2026, when Barclays Capital Real Estate, the original lender, made a $34,400,000 loan to two borrowers, Milton 90 Pleasant Valley Street LLC and Development Associates of Benton Harbor LLC.
The suit says the note carried a fixed interest rate of 6.400% and ran to a maturity date of May 6, 2036, with payments due on the sixth of each month.
The trustee says it was assigned into the trust effective May 20, 2026, the securitization step that places a loan into a CMBS pool.
It says two of the loan's guarantors filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey on or about June 4, 2026, and that the borrowers missed the first monthly payment, due June 6, 2026.
Under the loan terms, according to the suit, both events counted as defaults, and the interest rate moved to a default rate of 11.400%.
The trustee says it issued a default letter dated June 16, 2026, followed by an acceleration letter dated July 15, 2026, the notice that makes the entire balance due at once.

editorial_room.why_now: This transaction is a data point on the cost and availability of construction debt for mid-scale transit-oriented projects in Chicago, a market where such deals are closely watched for signs of lender appetite.
editorial_room.favored_thesis: The loan's terms—size, LTC, and inclusion of acquisition costs—reflect a lender's bet that transit proximity and a mix of market-rate and affordable units will mitigate lease-up risk, even with a 2027 delivery.
alternate_angles: The $28.3M loan as a signal of Associated Bank's regional lending strategy in multifamily.
The project's 15% affordable set-aside as a mechanism for zoning or tax incentives, not just altruism.
The former Tortenson Glass Co. site as a case study in urban infill land valuation.
skeptic_objections: Single transaction, not a market trend; one lender's appetite does not indicate a shift.
No details on loan terms (rate, LTC, recourse) to assess risk pricing.
The 2027 completion date is far out; execution risk is high.
reporting_gaps: Loan terms (interest rate, LTC, recourse) are not disclosed.
No independent confirmation of the transaction from a second source.
Developer equity contribution and pre-leasing status unknown.
editorial_room.human_stakes: For the developers, the loan enables a 5-year project with execution risk; for future tenants, it adds 99 units in a transit-served area, with 15 affordable units.
editorial_room.concrete_detail: The loan includes funds to acquire the former Tortenson Glass Co., a 30,000 sq ft infill site, and will result in a five-story building with 99 units (84 market-rate, 15 affordable) and unit mix of studios, one-bedrooms, and two-bedrooms averaging 500, 750, and 1,150 sq ft respectively.
